title: Round 8 - re-selection under the reference-signal rule
focus: Rounds 6 and 7 selected the desk's four cards as if they were one combined portfolio, using correlation and holdings-overlap caps that round 7's own correction found cost real out-of-sample return. Round 8 retires that premise and treats each of the four cards as an independent reference signal that nobody combines.
headline: The round's own ranking picked B3-concentrated for the momentum seat on its stronger out-of-sample return, but the desk owner overrode it and seated B-momentum instead, on the grounds that B-momentum has never ranked worse than third across three separate historical matrices.
outcome:
The return-correlation cap, the holdings-overlap cap and the book veto were retired outright, not amended, on the stated reasoning that the desk owner reads each of the four cards as an independent reference signal for what to buy in a single real account - nobody holds all four at once, so there is nothing to veto.

In their place: at most one card per discipline and at most one per base family, plus two carried-over gates (positive median annualized adjusted excess at both the 5-year and 10-year rungs against both benchmarks, and at least one trade in the out-of-sample window). Ranking among survivors was by out-of-sample adjusted excess versus QQQ, taking the best card in each distinct discipline or family group.

Eight cards cleared both gates, the same eight round 6 found, spanning exactly four groups, so the ranking determined the roster without further tie-break. The rule's own output selected B3-concentrated for the momentum seat at roughly +40% out-of-sample adjusted excess against B-momentum's roughly +21%.

The desk owner seated B-momentum instead, weighting the evidence that it has never been worse than third across three different historical matrices and posts a better ten-year figure against both benchmarks. The document records this explicitly as an override rather than folding it into the rule, stating that both readings are supported by the programme's own numbers and neither is obviously wrong.

A benchmark-anchoring artifact was also found and explained rather than corrected as an error: recomputed SPY figures for the same cards differ from round 6's published figures by small amounts because the engine's own benchmark_return is measured over sessions actually traded, while a calendar-date recomputation is not - one benchmark measured two defensible ways.
owner_override: The round's own ranking selected B3-concentrated for the momentum seat on out-of-sample adjusted excess versus QQQ (roughly +40% against B-momentum's roughly +21%), but the desk owner overrode this and seated B-momentum instead, weighting the evidence that B-momentum has never finished worse than third across the round-2, round-4 and round-5-ladder matrices and posts the stronger ten-year figure against both benchmarks. The document records this explicitly as an override rather than folding it into the rule.
carries_forward: The momentum-seat override should become a pre-registered rule (a rank-stability gate, or a ranking on the 5y/10y ladder rungs) rather than remain a standing override, per the round's own closing instruction.
Whether StrategyCard.discipline is the right distinctness axis is unresolved - C-trend versus H-trend-diversified is named as the specific pairing it may be wrongly excluding.
The benchmark anchor (session-traded engine figure versus calendar-date recomputation) should be stated explicitly wherever a SPY figure crosses a round boundary.
Fix 4 (scoring the live desk's own matrix, weighted above backtests) is closer still and should keep being pursued.
